SHAP explanation report: U.S. IPO underpricing

Every value is in probability units (percentage points, pp, of the predicted probability that an IPO is underpriced). Values are out-of-sample: each fold's model explains that fold's test IPOs (expanding window, ALL-pillars feature set). For each IPO, base value + sum of SHAP values = predicted probability.

Reading the charts. Bars show the average absolute effect of each feature. In the dot plots every dot is an IPO: position = how much the feature moved that IPO's predicted probability, colour = the feature's value (red high, blue low).

Caveats. SHAP shows what the model relies on, not what causes underpricing; correlated features share credit; the models are class-weighted so base values sit near 0.5.
